title: Two minor pieces
tagline: Bishops mate, knights don't, and one pair is homework

principles.prompt: Which pairs of minor pieces can force mate against a lone king?
principles.answer: Two bishops: yes, comfortably. Bishop + knight: yes, but it's one of the hardest wins in chess. Two knights: no — it can't be forced.

principles.prompt: Two bishops against a lone king — what's the winning picture?
principles.answer: Bishops side by side form a diagonal wall; your king herds the enemy king to any corner, and the wall closes there. Mate always arrives in a corner.

principles.prompt: Bishop + knight — what do you need to know at this level?
principles.answer: The win is real but must finish in a corner of the bishop's colour, and it can take over thirty moves. Know the verdict; don't volunteer to prove it — and don't trade into it casually.

principles.prompt: Two knights against a lone king — verdict?
principles.answer: Draw. Every mating try runs through stalemate first, so it cannot be forced. If you're simplifying, keep something better than two knights.

principles.prompt: The enemy king sits in the corner with no moves. What must you check before any quiet move?
principles.answer: Stalemate. No moves plus no check means the game is drawn on the spot — in these endings every quiet move needs that one-second check first.

demos.title: The wall closes
demos.intro: The herding is done: Black's king is at the edge, White's king stands guard. Watch the two-bishop wall close in three moves.

steps.note: The light bishop seals the g8-diagonal — check.
f8 belongs to the dark bishop on a3, f7 to the king. Only the corner is left.
The dark bishop slides onto the long diagonal: mate. Side-by-side bishops make a wall no king slips through — and every mate in this ending looks like this corner picture.

demos.title: Two knights, no cigar
demos.intro: Same herding, knights instead — and the net has a hole that can't be sewn shut.

steps.note: Check — the king is pushed toward the corner, just like the bishop ending.
So far so good. Now White wants to cover f8 and h8 and give check, all at once…
The second knight joins with check —

— and the king strolls out the side door. To close it, White would first need a quiet move with Black boxed in: stalemate. That's the whole story — two knights can chase forever, but the mate can't be forced.

tests.title: Close the wall
tests.intro: The king is cornered and out of moves — which cuts both ways. One move wins; nearly everything else is a draw.

wrong.Bc5: Stalemate! Black's king has no moves — a quiet move here throws away the whole ending.
wrong.Bf4: Stalemate! Black's king has no moves — a quiet move here throws away the whole ending.
wrong.Kf6: Your king was guarding the h7-bishop — Kxh7, and king plus one bishop can't mate: draw.
wrong.Kf5: Your king was guarding the h7-bishop — Kxh7, and king plus one bishop can't mate: draw.
wrong.Bg8: Hanging the bishop — Kxg8, and one bishop can't mate: draw.

hints: Quiet moves are stalemate and king moves drop the h7-bishop. What's left?
Be5 — onto the long dark diagonal. Check, corner covered, wall closed: mate.

tests.explanationAfter: The corner picture: light bishop holds g8, king holds g7 and h7, and the dark bishop lands on the long diagonal with mate. Every two-bishop mate ends in this shape — and every quiet move a square away from it is stalemate.

tests.title: Any corner will do
tests.intro: Same wall, opposite corner. The bishops don't care which corner — the picture is identical.

wrong.Bc5: Stalemate! Black's king has no moves — check for that before every quiet move in this ending.
wrong.Bf4: Stalemate! Black's king has no moves — check for that before every quiet move in this ending.
wrong.Kc3: Your king was guarding the a2-bishop — Kxa2, and one bishop can't mate: draw.
wrong.Kc2: Your king was guarding the a2-bishop — Kxa2, and one bishop can't mate: draw.
wrong.Bb1: Hanging the bishop — Kxb1, and one bishop can't mate: draw.

hints: The a2-bishop seals b1, your king seals b2 — the box is built. Which diagonal delivers the check?
Bd4 — the long dark diagonal into a1. Mate.

tests.explanationAfter: Rotated 180 degrees, nothing changes: one bishop and the king build the box, the other bishop sweeps the long diagonal. Learn the picture once and you own all four corners.

tests.title: The light corner
tests.intro: This corner is light, so the roles swap: the dark bishop builds the box, the light one strikes.

wrong.Bd3: Stalemate! Black's king has no moves — a quiet move is half a point gone.
wrong.Bc4: Stalemate! Black's king has no moves — a quiet move is half a point gone.
wrong.Kf4: Your king was guarding the h2-bishop — Kxh2, and one bishop can't mate: draw.
wrong.Bg1: Hanging the bishop — Kxg1, and one bishop can't mate: draw.

hints: h1 is a light square, so the light bishop must deliver it. The dark bishop and your king already hold g1, g2 and h2.
Bf3 — down the long light diagonal into h1. Mate.

tests.explanationAfter: The corner's colour picks the striker: light corner, light bishop. Roles swap, picture stays — box from one bishop and the king, killing diagonal from the other.

tests.title: Four corners, one picture
tests.intro: Last corner. By now your hand should move by itself — but so should the stalemate check.

wrong.Be6: Stalemate! Black's king has no moves — the quiet move is the only way to lose from here.
wrong.Bf5: Stalemate! Black's king has no moves — the quiet move is the only way to lose from here.
wrong.Kc5: Your king was guarding the a7-bishop — Kxa7, and one bishop can't mate: draw.
wrong.Bb8: Hanging the bishop — Kxb8, and one bishop can't mate: draw.

hints: a8 is light: the d7-bishop strikes, everything else just has to keep standing still.
Bc6 — through b7 into a8. Mate.

tests.explanationAfter: Fourth corner, same three jobs: king guards the flight squares, one bishop plugs the edge, the other lands the diagonal blow. That's the whole two-bishop ending — herd to any corner and close the wall.
